title: Matrix and Linear Algebra Solver — Overview and definition
t: Matrix and Linear Algebra Solver — Overview and definition
description: Solves linear systems, least-squares, and eigenproblems exactly and numerically.
body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. Solves linear systems, least-squares, and eigenproblems exactly and numerically. A matrix and linear algebra solver handles Ax=b, least-squares min||Ax-b||, eigenvalue problems, and matrix functions for dense and sparse systems up to millions of unknowns. Real implementations wrap LAPACK for dense problems and SuiteSparse/PETSc iterative solvers (CG, GMRES, BiCGSTAB) with preconditioners for sparse ones. It selects direct vs iterative methods from matrix structure and reports residuals and condition estimates.
capabilities: Direct solves via LU, Cholesky, and QR for dense systems
Iterative Krylov solvers with ILU/AMG preconditioners for sparse systems
Symmetric and general eigenproblems, SVD, and pseudoinverses
Automatic method selection from sparsity pattern and conditioning
Residual, backward-error, and condition-number reporting

title: Matrix and Linear Algebra Solver — Actual implementation
t: Matrix and Linear Algebra Solver — Actual implementation
description: Solves linear systems, least-squares, and eigenproblems exactly and numerically.
body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. How Matrix and Linear Algebra Solver is actually implemented. A matrix and linear algebra solver handles Ax=b, least-squares min||Ax-b||, eigenvalue problems, and matrix functions for dense and sparse systems up to millions of unknowns. Real implementations combine Python/MATLAB-style API, C++ template API (Eigen), PETSc KSP interface, CLI with LAPACK, a sparse direct solver (SuiteSparse), MPI for distributed builds. The implementation is verified by Verify on the Florida Sparse Matrix Collection: residuals below tolerance, and known eigenpairs of reference matrices reproduced to documented precision

body: Public edition. Public tool knowledge, fact-checked reference. Teaching ladder for Matrix and Linear Algebra Solver, simple to complex. Rank 1: name the tool's single core action (Direct solves via LU, Cholesky, and QR for dense systems). Rank 3: run it once on a tiny input and check the output. Rank 5: combine two capabilities: Direct solves via LU, Cholesky, and QR for dense systems and Iterative Krylov solvers with ILU/AMG preconditioners for sparse systems. Rank 7: chain its output into a neighboring tool (Numerical computation engine) with a verification checkpoint. Rank 9+: automate the full workflow and teach it to someone else.
